_readme: Machine-readable run blocks for Banco, keyed by beat id. The prompt TEXT is never here - it lives in demo-prompts.json, vendored from the deck (docs/adr/0001). This file holds only what a program needs in order to execute a beat: how many panes, which kind of model source each pane wants, the sampling parameters the room must see, and which file is pasted in. Merged over the demo database at load time by app/server/runs.py, so the vendored copy stays byte-identical to its pin. See docs/adr/0003.
_roles_note: A pane asks for a ROLE, never a named provider. 'primary' and 'secondary' are two different API providers; 'local' is Ollama. The profile chosen at first run binds roles to concrete providers, which is what lets a missing source degrade a beat to replay instead of removing it (PROJECT.md, Configuration model). A run block that named 'anthropic' would break the offline profile and could not degrade.
_teaches_params_note: The parameters a beat exists to expose. They are what a collapsed pane shows with no gesture; everything else sits behind the Info control (docs/specs/model-control.md §6). Absent or empty is legal and means "nothing to foreground" - the safe default, because a pane showing no parameter makes no claim about it. Every value must be one of Banco's four parameter names (temperature, max_tokens, system, think) and must actually be stated by a pane of that beat; tests/test_precedence.py fails otherwise.
_temperature_note: Temperature is stated explicitly on every pane because the room has to see it - that is objective 2, and it is why m1-p3 was a dead branch on consumer products. The value is data, not code: change it here.

m1-p1.teaches: Sampling variance, and that fields absent from the source get filled anyway.
m1-p1.teaches_it: La varianza di campionamento, e il fatto che i campi assenti dalla fonte vengono comunque riempiti.
m1-p1._panes_note: Two samples from each of two sources, because this beat teaches two things at once: the same model disagrees with itself (panes 0 vs 1, 2 vs 3), and two models disagree with each other (A vs B). PROJECT.md records D1 as only 'partly' local-capable for exactly this reason - sampling works with one source, cross-source disagreement does not.

m1-p2.teaches: Asked for its source, the model either admits it inferred the value or points at a passage that is not there.
m1-p2.teaches_it: Interrogato sulla sua fonte, il modello o ammette di aver dedotto il valore o indica un passaggio che non c'è.
m1-p2._continues_note: The deck says 'the same chat, right after'. Each pane carries its own m1-p1 exchange forward as conversation history, so pane 2 is asked about what pane 2 wrote. Restarting the conversation here would destroy the beat: there would be no prior entry to interrogate.

m2-p1.teaches: Capability differs by model: the same prompt, over the same four drafts, gets a deeper judgement from a larger model.
m2-p1.teaches_it: La capacita' cambia col modello: lo stesso prompt, sulle stesse quattro bozze, ottiene da un modello piu' grande un giudizio piu' profondo.
m2-p1._panes_note: Two panes, not four: D2 inverts D1's shape. D1 gives one input to four panes to show them disagreeing; D2 gives the same one input to two panes to show them differing in DEPTH. The labels are deliberately neutral - 'Giudice A' and 'Giudice B', never 'small' and 'large' - because which is which is a property of the session profile, not of this file, and a pane captioned 'modello piccolo' beside whatever the profile happened to bind would be a false statement on a projected screen. The model id on each pane carries the fact, and it is true by construction.

inputs._append_note: This prompt has no [PASTE ...] hole: it says 'these four drafts' and expects them to be in the conversation, because in the room a person pastes them under the question. So the file is appended rather than substituted. See app/server/runs.build_prompt.

m2-p2.teaches: Deliberation is a budget, not a switch: the same model, the same question, once with no reasoning budget and once with one.
m2-p2.teaches_it: La deliberazione e' un budget, non un interruttore: stesso modello, stessa domanda, una volta senza budget di ragionamento e una volta con.
m2-p2._panes_note: Both panes ask the SAME role, so both bind to the same provider and the same model. The only difference between them is the reasoning budget, which is the whole beat: two panes on two different models would show capability again, which is what beat 1 already showed. `max_tokens` is stated because a budget has to fit under it - Anthropic requires 1024 <= budget < max_tokens - so the ceiling is part of what this beat asks for and not a detail of the configuration.
m2-p2._think_note: The budget is stated as an INTEGER because that is the claim: deliberation is a budget. Anthropic sends it as thinking.budget_tokens and Google as thinking_budget. Ollama and OpenAI take levels instead, so on those the parameter is DROPPED and the pane says so - honest, but the beat then does not demonstrate its mechanism. That is what the pre-flight capability check is for: bind `primary` for m2 to a budget-capable source before this beat runs.

_unblocked_note: Every beat in the demo database that Banco cannot yet execute, and why. tests/test_run_blocks.py fails if an active beat appears in neither this map nor 'beats', so 'the demo exists but Banco cannot run it' cannot go unnoticed - which is the condition Banco was built to end.
_language_note: Banco speaks Italian by default and English second. Every string in this file that reaches a surface carries both: the bare field is English and `<field>_it` is Italian, matching the convention of the vendored demo database. That is `teaches` / `teaches_it`, a pane's `label` / `label_it`, and the `_unblocked` / `_unblocked_it` maps. app/i18n.localized is the only code that knows the rule; nothing else may append '_it' to a field name. An untranslated entry falls back to English rather than disappearing, and tests/test_i18n.py reports which ones are still missing.
_inputs_note: `replaces` is the placeholder in the English prompt and `replaces_it` the one in the Italian prompt. They are different strings — the deck writes '[PASTE RAW NOTES]' and '[INCOLLA APPUNTI GREZZI]' — so a single value would leave the pasted file unsubstituted in one language and send the model a literal placeholder. tests/test_i18n.py checks every input against the prompt it is meant to fill, in both languages.
